name: Trade war & tariffs
value: US Section 301 tariffs on 16 partners pending
summary: US expected to announce Section 301 tariffs on 16 partners including China and the EU; rates not yet confirmed
state: US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer was expected to announce new Section 301 tariffs on 16 trading partners, including China, the EU, Mexico and Japan, as soon as 24 Nov, to replace tariffs the Supreme Court struck down; China is likely to face higher rates on average and steel and aluminium are expected to be excluded (The Fiscal Times). The excess-capacity probes began on 11 Mar (CNBC). No final rates, start dates or retaliation were found to 25 Nov, so Watch holds; Alert needs broad tariffs in force with retaliation.
for_you: Importers and exporters trading with the US face uncertainty over rates and start dates until USTR publishes its notice. UK firms can follow Department for Business and Trade guidance on US tariffs.
rubric_hit: Watch: major new tariffs threatened between large economies (Section 301 on China, EU, Japan, Mexico); not yet in force, no retaliation

sources.title: The Fiscal Times — Trump Readies New Tariff Hikes for Dozens of Countries
CNBC — Trump administration launches Section 301 trade probes into Mexico, China, EU, others

why: Tariffs raise prices, reroute supply chains and slow growth; escalation cycles hurt export-heavy economies like the UK's partners.
drivers: US tariff policy, retaliation, court rulings, trade deals, WTO disputes.

rubric.alert: Broad new tariffs in force with retaliation under way, or US average effective tariff rising sharply.
rubric.watch: New major tariffs announced or threatened between large economies.
rubric.normal: Tariff regime stable; no new major measures in the past two weeks.
